The bill is now before Senate Ways and Means. The bill pages give no operative text, so covered software, prohibited conduct, penalties and effective date are not stated.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21, An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases (barred from November 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: This proposed statewide ballot measure would have struck G.L. c. 40P, the statewide prohibition on rent control. In its place it would have capped any annual rent increase for covered dwelling units at the lower of the annual Consumer Price Index increase or five percent. On June 23, 2026 the SJC held in Cella v. Attorney General that the petition relates to religion under art. 48, because it exempts facilities operated solely for religious purposes. The court remanded for a judgment enjoining placement of the petition on the November 2026 ballot.
rules.key_value: Proposed cap: lower of annual CPI increase or 5% (never took effect)

new_construction_exemption.basis: newly constructed units less than 10 years old (per secondary source DX14)

unverifiable_exemptions: dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes
coverage.summary: The cap would have applied to all 'covered dwelling units' statewide. The official opinion names one exclusion: facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes. A secondary source adds four more: owner-occupied buildings of four or fewer units, units under 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, and short-term rentals. The petition would have repealed G.L. c. 40P.
coverage.owner_conditions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units exempt (per DX14).

rules.exemptions: Facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes (official opinion). Per a secondary source, also: owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, and short-term rentals.
rules.effective_date_note: Never took effect. The SJC decision of June 23, 2026 bars placement on the November 2026 statewide ballot.
citation_aliases: An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.quoted_span: The petition, if enacted, would end the Statewide prohibition on rent control "by striking out [G. L. c. 40P]" and instituting in its place "a limit on any annual rent increase" set at "the annual increase in Consumer Price Index or [five percent], whichever is lower."
rules.review_note: The petition's full text is not captured, and the opinion describes its terms only partly. Exemptions other than the educational/religious/nonprofit facilities come only from a secondary blog. Proponents say the defect is 'easily fixable' and hinted at a 2028 petition, but no refiling is documented. G.L. c. 40P, the state ban on local rent control, therefore remains in force; it is not a rent-cap record.
rules.source_notes: Primary source is the SJC opinion (DX03). DX14 (law blog) and DX15 (WBUR) describe the same decision.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.

The petition included several exemptions, including owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, newly constructed units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
The state’s Supreme Judicial Court ruled a ballot question seeking to bring rent control back to Massachusetts cannot go forward this November, because it includes a religious exemption.

rules.title: Ban on discrimination against public assistance and housing subsidy recipients (G.L. c. 151B, § 4(10))
rules.requirement: It is an unlawful practice for any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against someone for either of two reasons. The first is that the person receives federal, state or local public assistance (including medical assistance) or housing subsidies (including rental assistance or rental supplements). The second is any requirement of such a program. Landlords therefore may not screen out or treat applicants or tenants differently on that basis.
rules.key_value: No discrimination against public-assistance or housing-subsidy (e.g. rental assistance) recipients, or because of program requirements

coverage.summary: Applies to any person furnishing rental accommodations, credit or services. Subsection 10 states no unit-count or owner-occupancy exemption.
coverage.other_conditions: Protects recipients of public assistance and tenants receiving housing subsidies.

rules.effective_date_note: The document does not state when subsection 10 took effect.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.
rules.review_note: Subsection 7B separately bars rental advertisements indicating a preference based on 'public assistance recipiency'. The owner-occupied two-family exemptions in subsections 7 and 11 are not stated for subsection 10. Boston and Cambridge have their own source-of-income protections, which are complementary.
rules.source_notes: Official statute text; no penalty or effective date in the section.

rules.title: Fourteen-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease (G.L. c. 186, § 11)
rules.requirement: If a tenant neglects or refuses to pay rent due under a written lease, 14 days' written notice to quit ends the lease. The tenant can defeat this by paying or tendering all rent due, with interest and costs, on or before the answer date in the possession action. If the nonpayment was caused by a government delay in mailing or delivering a subsistence or rental payment, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days. It must then treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent, interest and costs are tendered within that time.
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment; cure by answer date; at least 7-day continuance for government payment delay

coverage.summary: Applies statewide to tenancies under a written lease where rent is unpaid.
coverage.other_conditions: Written leases; nonpayment of rent only.

rules.effective_date_note: The text gives no effective date. The section is current codified law.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.
rules.review_note: This is a termination-notice rule, not a list of just causes. Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause list in the documents.

rules.title: Notice to terminate a tenancy at will (G.L. c. 186, § 12)
rules.requirement: Either party may end a tenancy at will with three months' written notice. If rent is payable at intervals shorter than three months, notice equal to the rental interval or 30 days, whichever is longer, is enough. For nonpayment of rent, 14 days' written notice to quit ends the tenancy. A tenant who has not received a similar notice in the prior 12 months can prevent termination by paying the full rent due within 10 days of receipt. Every nonpayment notice must include the statutory right-to-cure notification. If it is omitted, the cure period extends to the answer date, but the notice stays valid. If nonpayment was caused by a government payment delay, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days.
rules.key_value: 3 months' written notice (or rental interval/30 days, whichever longer); 14 days for nonpayment; 10-day cure once per 12 months; mandatory cure-notice text

rules.review_note: This sets termination-notice periods. It does not list just causes, so a tenancy at will can be ended without cause on proper notice.

rules.title: State tenant-rights form must accompany a notice to quit for nonpayment (G.L. c. 186, § 31)
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent to a residential tenant must be accompanied by a form. The form must include documentation of any repayment agreements. It must also give information on rental assistance programs (including RAFT), applicable trial court rules and orders for summary process, and federal or state eviction restrictions. It must prominently state that the notice to quit is not an eviction, the tenant need not leave immediately, the tenant is entitled to a legal proceeding, and only a court order can force the tenant to leave. The executive office of housing and livable communities develops and posts the form. The clause (ii) information must be available in the 5 most common languages besides English. Courts, including the Boston municipal court department, may not accept a nonpayment summary process filing without proof of delivery of the form.
rules.key_value: Required state form with nonpayment notice to quit; no court filing without proof of delivery; information in English plus 5 most common languages

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit law (G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
rules.requirement:
A security deposit may not exceed the first month's rent. Holding rules:
- Hold it in a separate interest-bearing account in a Massachusetts bank, beyond the reach of the lessor's creditors.
- Give a bank receipt within 30 days.
- Give a signed deposit receipt, and a statement of condition upon receipt or within 10 days after the tenancy starts, whichever is later.
- Pay 5% annual interest, or the lesser bank rate, each year.

Return rules:
- Return the deposit or balance within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
- Deductions are limited to unpaid rent or water charges, unpaid tax escalations, and reasonable damage beyond wear and tear.
- Damage deductions need a sworn itemized list.

Other rules:
- Keep records for 2 years.
- On transfer, the successor must take over the deposit and notify the tenant within 45 days.
- Violations forfeit the right to retain the deposit and carry treble damages plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees.
- Lease waivers are void.
- Under the version effective August 1, 2025, EOHLC may authorize by regulation an optional fee in lieu of a deposit. Fee plus deposit may not exceed 1 month's rent in total.
rules.key_value: Max deposit = first month's rent; return within 30 days; 5% interest (or lesser bank rate); treble damages; fee in lieu plus deposit capped at 1 month's rent

rules.title: Broker fee paid only by the party who engaged the broker (G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD½)
rules.requirement: No one may engage in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee unless licensed as a broker or salesperson. A licensed broker or salesperson may contract solely with the prospective tenant or solely with the landlord or landlord's agent. Any fee must be paid only by the party, lessor or tenant, who originally engaged and contracted with the broker or salesperson.
